name: three-part-lesson-designer
description: Design a Montessori three-period lesson for introducing concepts through concrete materials and naming. Use when teaching vocabulary, classifications, or concepts through hands-on materials.
evidence_sources: Lillard (2012) — Preschool children's development in classic Montessori, supplemented Montessori, and conventional programs
Lillard (2005) — Montessori: The Science Behind the Genius
Séguin (1866) — Idiocy: and its treatment by the physiological method (origin of the three-period lesson)
Standing (1957) — Maria Montessori: Her Life and Work (detailed description of three-period lesson)

required.description: The specific concept, vocabulary, or classification the lesson will introduce — what students need to learn to name, recognise, and recall
The physical materials or objects that will be used — what students will see and handle during the lesson

optional.description: How many students — typically 1-3 in Montessori practice
What students already know about this concept or related concepts
Any language needs — EAL students, technical vocabulary, or multiple languages in the classroom

fields.description: The complete lesson across all three periods — naming, recognition, and recall
How to prepare and present the materials — including isolation of the concept
How to know when the student has mastered each period — the observable evidence of understanding
Activities for students who master the lesson quickly and activities for students who need additional practice
